yearNumbering: astronomical (0 = 1 BCE); sourceStartYear/sourceEndYear retain original Pleiades historical numbering without year zero
temporalPolicy: Ancient markers show possible relevance within the selected source location year envelope. This is approximate period relevance, not proof of continuous occupation. Modern context markers have no historical validity; show only when explicitly enabled and label as modern orientation.
spatialPolicy: Point locations only; neither territorial extent, city size nor population. Ancient point accuracy is source reported. Natural Earth is generalized 1:10m cartography, not street-level data.
selectionPolicy: Settlement-tagged place; certain identity; one precise, certain direct point with reported accuracy <=2000 m. Select minimum accuracy radius then source URI, retaining only that location chronology. No importance/population rank inferred.

sources.title: Pleiades Datasets 4.1
sources.attribution: Pleiades contributors; Ancient World Mapping Center and Institute for the Study of the Ancient World. Pleiades Datasets 4.1 (28 May 2025). Each point links to its place and selected location; original provenance remains in the retained exact GIS CSVs.
sources.changes: Filter settlement types, certain identity and precise direct points; select one location; convert no-year-zero source years; compact browser fields. No source geometry edits or ownership assertions.

The city was the seat of a bishopric in the Byzantine period and was the last of Morocco's cities to recognize the authority of the emperor at the time of the Arab conquest.

places.description: Regium Lepidum (modern Reggio Emilia) was founded by M. Aemilius Lepidus in either 187 or 175 B.C.

places.title: Segesta Tigulliorum
places.description: Coastal settlement of the Ligures Tigullii.

places.title: Sibrium
places.description: The Roman fort of Sibrium, known today as Castelseprio or Castel Seprio, became a significant Lombard town of the early Middle Ages. It was destroyed and abandoned in 1287. In 2011, the site, including the church of Santa Maria 'foris portas', the castrum and its Torba Tower, was enrolled as a UNESC

places.title: Sirmio
places.description: Modern Sirmione on Lake Garda.

places.title: Tannetum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 39 G4 Tannetum

places.title: Ticinum
places.description: An ancient city of Gallia Transpadana, Ticinum lay along the line of the ancient Via Aemilia. Today Ticinum is the modern city of Pavia.

places.description: An ancient settlement that began as a second century B.C. Roman military outpost.

places.title: Veleia
places.description: Veleia was an ancient Ligurian settlement (regio VIII).

places.title: Vercellae
places.description: Originally a captial of the Libici, a tribe of Ligurians, Vercellae became an important Roman municipium.

places.title: Unit IV-1 at Nichoria
places.description: Unit IV-1 is a large, megaron-style building constructed during the 11th century BCE at the site of Nichoria in Messenia, Greece.

places.title: Tell Um Hammad Sharqi
places.description: Archaeological site on the banks of the Zerqa River with signs of habitation in the Early Bronze Age I-II and IV. The eastern portion of the larger Tell Um Hammad site is called Um Hammad Sharqiya; the western section is Um Hammad al-Gharbi. The two may have been linked as a single village in the Ea

places.title: Eilean Dòmhnuill
places.description: Eilean Dòmhnuill is the site of perhaps the earliest crannog settlement in Scotland.

places.title: Cortaillod-Est
places.description: Settlement on the northern shore of Lake Neuchâtel in Switzerland containing the inundated remains of a Bronze Age village, inhabited ca. 1010-955 BC.

places.title: Casian
places.description: An unnamed settlement close to the modern village of Casian is also not far from the rock inscriptions from the Șeremet forest. The rock inscriptions mention the limits of the community of the Kasians and their caves. A house from the Roman period and some coins were found here. The relation between

places.title: Adana
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 B3 Adana

places.title: Adane/Athenae/Eudaimon Arabia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C3 Adane/Athenae/Eudaimon Arabia

places.title: Adedou Kome

places.title: Adouli
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 A2 Adouli

places.title: Akila/Okelis
places.description: A coastal station or anchorage and associated settlement that scholars identify with the modern Khawr/Khor Ghurayrah on Yemen's Ra’s Shaykh Sa‘īd headland in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. This small bay is almost closed by sand and coral reefs today. The precise location of the ancient settlement is not

places.title: Anagrana/Negram
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 B2 Anagrana/Negram

places.title: Athroula/Laththa
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 B2 Athroula/Laththa

places.title: Caminacum
places.description: Caminacum was an ancient settlement of South Arabia. Its ruins, located in Yemen's Al Jawf Governorate, are known today as Kamna.

places.title: Cariati
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C2 Cariati

places.title: Caripeta
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C3 Caripeta

places.title: Deire
places.description: Deire is located on a promontory (modern Ras Siyyan) on the western side of the Bab-el-Mandeb strait, located between the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

places.title: Acelum
places.description: Acelum (modern Asolo) was an ancient settlement of the Veneti.

places.title: Altinum
places.description: Altinum was the capital of the Veneti of northern Italy. The site was destroyed by Attila in AD 452.

places.title: Ariminum
places.description: Ariminum (Rimini) is a Roman colony founded on the Adriatic coast in 268 BC.

places.title: Ateste
places.description: Ateste was a city of northern Italy, located in the interior of Venetia.

places.title: Brundulum

places.title: Fabbrica dei Soci
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A2 Fabbrica dei Soci

places.title: Faventia
places.description: A Roman city on the Via Aemilia.

places.title: Felsina/Bononia
places.description: A city of the Po Plain with important cultural phases related to Etruscan, Celtic, and Roman culture. Important evidence for the Iron Age Villanovan culture has been found in Bononia and its vicinity. The Romans established a Latin colony of 3000 settlers at Bononia in 189 BC. After changing hands s

places.title: [Feraria]
places.description: The early settlement history of [Feraria] (modern Ferrara) remains uncertain. The name Ferrara appears in AD 753 in a document of the Lombard king Desiderius.

places.title: Fondo Paviani
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A2 Fondo Paviani

places.title: Forum Cornelii
places.description: An ancient city founded by Lucius Cornelius Sulla as a colony ca. 82 BC.

places.title: Forum Gallorum
places.description: A town on the Via Aemilia that was the site of a battle waged between M. Antonius and Hirtius and Pansa during the siege of Mutina.

places.title: Forum Livii
places.description: The town of Forum Livii in Gallia Cispadana is located on the right bank of the Montone River.

places.title: Forum Popilii
places.description: Forum Popilii on the Via Aemilia was founded in 173 BC by M. Popilius Laenas.

places.title: Frattesina
places.description: Frattesina di Rovigo is the site of Final Bronze Age (FBA) occupation, ca. 1200–1000 B.C.

places.title: (H)Atria
places.description: (H)Atria (modern Adria) was a Venetic and, later, Etruscan settlement. The city itself is likely a sixth century BC foundation.

places.title: [(H)Eraclia]
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 D1 [(H)Eraclia]

places.title: Iulia Concordia
places.description: Iulia Concordia (Concordia Sagittaria) was established by the Romans in 42 BC at the intersection of the Via Annia and the Via Postumia.

places.title: Ligeris
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 A1 Ligeris

places.title: Kainua
places.description: An Etruscan town in the plain of the Po river at modern Marzabotto. It was founded in the early fifth century B.C.

places.title: Mons Silicis
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 B2 Mons Silicis

places.title: Opitergium
places.description: Opitergium (modern Oderzo) is a settlement of the Veneti along the Piave River located at a junction of the Via Postumia.

places.title: Patavium
places.description: An ancient settlement of the Veneti, Patavium became a Roman municipium in 45 BC. It was the birthplace of several famous Romans including Titus Livius, Valerius Flaccus, Asconius Pedianus and Thrasea Paetus.

places.title: Portus Liquentiae
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 D1 Portus Liquentiae

places.title: Portus Reatinus
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 D1 Portus Reatinus

places.title: Ravenna
places.description: A city of northern Adriatic Italy that served as the capital of the Western Roman Empire from A.D. 402 until 476.

places.title: Tarvisium
places.description: Tarvisium (Treviso) is a settlement located in the plain of the Silis river, not far from the Via Claudia Augusta.

places.title: [Torcellum]
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 40 C2 [Torcellum]

places.title: Vicetia
places.description: Vicetia (modern Vicenza) as a settlement of the Veneti in northern Italy.

places.title: Malao

places.title: Mari(a)ba
places.description: Capital of the Sabaean kingdom.

places.title: Marimatha
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C3 Marimatha

places.title: Sabat(h)a
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C2 Sabat(h)a

places.title: Ẓafār
places.description: This ancient settlement, located in the southern highlands of modern Yemen, was the capital of the Ḥimyarite tribal confederacy from the third to the sixth centuries of the modern era.

places.title: Save
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 B3 Save

places.title: Tamna
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C2 Tamna

places.title: Thialemath
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 D2 Thialemath

places.title: Tretos
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 4 C3 Tretos

places.title: Zabida
places.description: The historical town of Zabid in Yemen is noted for its architecture. It served as the capital of Yemen from the 13th to the 15th century and played an important role in the Arab and Muslim world for many centuries because of its Islamic university.

places.title: Tal-i-iblis
places.description: Tell in the Bard Sir Valley in Iran occupied in the late 4th-early 3rd millennia BCE. This site was an important place for copper smelting from its earliest period of occupation. The site has been largely destroyed by mining.

places.title: Tawilan
places.description: Settlement near the village of Tawilan, Jordan, just west of Petra, with archaeological remains from the Iron Age and Persian period. Notably, there is no evidence of Nabataean occupation at this site despite its proximity to Petra.

places.title: Kephala
places.description: A Neolithic site and cemetery on Keos.

places.title: Allahdino
places.description: A settlement located some 40km outside of modern Karachi, Pakistan, dating to the Mature Harappan period. The site was abandoned by the close of the third millennium BCE.

places.title: ‘Argoos Limen’
places.description: A port on the island of Ilva (modern Elba), so named based on the resting place of the Argonauts, according to Strabo.

places.title: Artimino
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 E2 Artimino

places.title: Castiglioncello
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 C3 Castiglioncello

places.title: Colle delle Carbonaie
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 C1 Colle delle Carbonaie

places.title: Falesia
places.description: A Tyrrhenian coastal port opposite Elba. Modern Piombino.

places.title: Fufluna/Populonium
places.description: Populonia likely derives its name from the Etruscan god 'Fufluns' and was an important maritime and commercial center of Etruria located in the Colline Metallifere.

places.title: Igilium (settlement and villa)
places.description: An ancient settlement and villa at modern Giglio Porto on the Italian island of Giglio.

places.title: Isola del Migliarino
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 C2 Isola del Migliarino

places.title: Lago dell’Accesa (archaeological site)
places.description: The archaeological site of Lago dell’Accesa, in the locality known as "La Pesta", is situated nearby the lake of Lago dell'Accesa. The site was situated so as to exploit local mineral resources and the archaeological remains provide extensive evidence for habitation from the ninth through sixth cent

places.title: Levigliani
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 C1 Levigliani

places.title: Luca
places.description: Luca (the modern Lucca) was originally an Etruscan settlement that became a Roman colony ca. 180 B.C.

places.title: Luna
places.description: Luna (the modern Luni) is an ancient settlement of Liguria. It was re-founded by the Romans as a colonial settlement in 177 BC.

places.title: Orbetello
places.description: A city of Tyrrhenian Etruria that came under Roman control in 280 B.C.; the Latin colony of Cosa was established nearby in 273 B.C.

places.title: Pescia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 D2 Pescia

places.title: Pisae
places.description: A city situated on the Tyrrhenian seaboard and likely of Etruscan origin. Its early nature was that of a mercantile center. The city became a Roman colony in 89 B.C.

places.title: Pistoriae
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 D2 Pistoriae

places.title: Ponte a Moriano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 D2 Ponte a Moriano

places.title: Portus Herculis
places.description: Portus Herculis is located on the eastern side of the Monte Argentario peninsula, about 40 km south-east of Grosseto and about 7 km south-west of Orbetello. and about 12 km from Porto Santo Stefano. The site is in use as a port in the Etruscan, Roman, and Late Antique phases of occupation. It is inc

places.title: Portus Veneris
places.description: A Roman maritime community that may derive its name from a local sanctuary of Venus, Portus Veneris served as the base of the Byzantine fleet until it was destroyed in A.D. 643.

places.title: S. Gaetano di Vada
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 C3 S. Gaetano di Vada

places.title: S. Maria del Giudice
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 C2 S. Maria del Giudice

places.title: S. Rocchino

places.title: Scarlino
places.description: A fortified Medieval site in the Maremma region of Italy with evidence for earlier fortified centers.

places.title: Telamon
places.description: An ancient city of coastal Etruria, Telamon was eventually razed by L. Cornelius Sulla.

places.title: Tempagnano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 41 D2 Tempagnano

places.title: Vatl/Vetulonia
places.description: The Etruscan Vatluna resisted Rome's influence in the seventh century BCE, although the city may have been the source of Rome's adoption of the curule chair and the fasces.

places.title: Velathri/Volaterrae
places.description: A major Etruscan city of North Etruria.

places.title: Lalibela
places.description: Lalibela is an ancient site in in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia known especially for its 11 rock-cut churches.

places.title: Woodcock Hall
places.description: Site of late Iron-Age and Romano-British settlement near present-day Saham Toney in Norfolk. An Neronian-era fort is directly adjacent.

places.title: Medina Azahara
places.description: The Caliphate City of Medina Azahara is a city built in the mid-tenth century CE by the Umayyad dynasty as the seat of the Caliphate of Cordoba.

places.title: Pyrgouthi
places.description: Settlement featuring a Hellenistic tower west of the cemetery in the Berbati Valley occupied from the Iron Age to the Early Roman period.

places.title: Agora of the Competaliasts or Hermaists
places.description: Originally a commercial area of ancient Delos, built in the second century BCE on artificial infill adjacent to the city's port. The function of this area seems to have changed after the expansion and consolidation of Roman rule, with residential construction taking over the original commercial acti

places.title: Aesis
places.description: An Umbrian town that became a colonia civium Romanorum under the name of Aesis in 247 B.C.

places.title: Allumiere
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Allumiere

places.title: Ameria
places.description: Ameria, claimed by Cato the Elder as the oldest town in Umbria, was an important center that may have gained Roman municipal status as early as 338 B.C., following the Latin War.

places.title: Amiternum
places.description: Amiternum was an ancient settlement of the Sabines that Rome captured in 293 BC. The settlement was situated at the intersection of four Roman roads: the Via Caecilia, the Via Claudia Nova, and the two branches of the Via Salaria. The historian Sallust was born at Amiternum in 86 B.C.

places.title: Ancon(a)
places.description: A port city founded by colonists from Syracuse in 387 BC.

places.title: Anguillara
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Anguillara

places.title: Anneianum
places.description: Anneianum was located in the Etruscan Apennines, along the road from Faventia to Florentia.

places.title: Anxanum
places.description: City of the Frentani, situated on a hill about 5 miles from the Adriatic Sea, and 8 miles from the mouth of the river Sagrus or Sangro in Italy.

places.title: Aquae Cutiliae
places.description: Roman city situated on mineral springs known today as Terme di Cotilia or Terme di Vespasiano in the Sabina region, Italy

places.title: Aquae Passeris
places.description: Located in Etruria, Aquae Passeris was frequented in antiquity for its thermal springs, as noted by Martial. The site is included on the Tabula Peutingeriana, placing it on the road from Rome to Volsinii. Its location likely corresponds to that of Bacucco, a comune to the north of Viterbo.

places.title: Arna
places.description: Arna was an ancient city of Umbria that was controlled by Etruscans in the fourth century BCE.

places.title: Arretium
places.description: Arretium (the Etruscan Aritim) was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae and described by Livy as one of the "Capitae Etruriae". The Romans captured the city in 311 B.C. and it became a station on the via Cassia.

places.title: Asciano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Asciano

places.title: Asculum
places.description: Asculum (modern Ascoli Piceno) was the principal city of the Piceni.

places.title: Asisium
places.description: A Roman settlement built atop an earlier Umbrian one on a western foothill of the Apennines, Asisium received municipal status and was assigned to the Tribus Sergia. Totila destroyed most of the city in A.D. 545.

places.title: Aternum
places.description: Aternum (modern Pescara) was a settlement at the mouth of the Aternus River.

places.title: Attidium
places.description: An ancient settlement of Umbria mentioned only by Pliny the Elder. Numerous inscriptions discovered at the site indicate that Attidium achieved the status of a municipium.

places.title: *Aufenginum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 *Aufenginum

places.title: Aufinum
places.description: Aufinum, long thought to have been located at modern Ofena, which reflects the ancient name, has been shown by recent excavations to have been located some 5km further south, near modern Capestrano. Aufinum was an ancient center of the Abruzzo. Pliny lists the Aufinates Cismontani among the communit

places.title: *Aurinia/Saturnia
places.description: An Etruscan town that Dionysius of Halicarnassus claimed had been founded by the Pelasgians, Saturnia received a Roman colony in 183 BC.

places.title: Auximum
places.description: Auximum (modern Osimo) is an ancient settlement of Picenum. The original foundation was likely carried out by Greeks from Ancona. The Romans made it a base for military operations from 174 B.C.

places.title: Aveia
places.description: Aveia was a settlement of the Vestini in the valley of the Aterno river.

places.title: Balneum Regis
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C3 Balneum Regis

places.title: Blera
places.description: Blera was a significant Etruscan settlement in the vicinity of Tarquinii. It lay along the line of the Roman Via Clodia. It received Roman municipal status and was enrolled in the tribus Arnensis. The city flourished in the sixth and fifth centuries BCE.

places.title: Caelanum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Caelanum

places.title: Cales
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Cales

places.title: Camerinum
places.description: Camerinum was a town in Umbria on the frontiers of Picenum that was allied to Rome from 309 B.C.

places.title: Campovalano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Campovalano

places.title: Capena
places.description: An ancient urban center in Faliscan territory adjacent to Etruria, Capena was sacked by the Romans in 390 BC.

places.title: Capestrano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Capestrano

places.title: Carsulae
places.description: An ancient settlement originating the late fourth or third centuries BC and lying along the route of the Roman Via Flaminia.

places.title: Casone
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Casone

places.title: Castellina
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 A2 Castellina

places.title: Castelluccio di Pienza
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelluccio di Pienza

places.title: Castellum Firmanorum
places.description: Castellum Firmanorum was the ancient port of Firmum Picenum.

places.title: Castelsecco
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B2 Castelsecco

places.title: Castro
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Castro

places.title: Castrum Novum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Novum

places.title: Castrum Truentinum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Castrum Truentinum

places.title: Centum Cellae
places.description: Centum Cellae (modern Civitavecchia) was an ancient coastal settlement in Tyrrhenian Etruria. The emperor Trajan re-builds the harbor at the site in 106/7 and Pliny the Younger mentions its name, Centum Cellae. Saracens destroyed the city in A.D. 812.

places.title: Chianciano Terme
places.description: Chianciano Terme begins as an Etruscan site, with a temple located near the natural springs. By the first century B.C. the site was popular with Romans as a healing spa.

places.title: Cingulum
places.description: Cingulum was a town in Picenum.

places.title: Civita
places.description: The Civita di Bagnoregio was originally founded by the Etruscans.

places.title: La Cività di Spedino
places.description: La Cività di Spedino was a fortified upland center (951 m ASL) in the territory of the Aequi.

places.title: Civitalba
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D2 Civitalba

places.title: Cluana
places.description: Cluana was an ancient settlement in Picenum.

places.title: Clusium
places.description: Clusium, the Etruscan Clevsin (modern Chiusi), was a major city of Etruria. Lars Porsena was a sixth century B.C. king of Clusium.

places.title: Cluviae
places.description: A city of the Carricini Samnites.

places.title: Contrada S. Rustico
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F3 Contrada S. Rustico

places.title: Corchiano
places.description: Corchiano was the site of a wealthy settlement in the Ager Faliscus that was in proximity to the Via Amerina.

places.title: Corciano
places.description: The environs of Corciano were inhabited by Etruscans and, later, there is evidence for Roman villas. In 1812, a series of bronze panels from an Etruscan parade chariot was discovered at Castel San Mariano di Corciano.

places.title: Cortona
places.description: An Umbrian city that, under Etruscan influence, expanded and came to be called 'Curtun'. Later it became the Roman colony of Cortino.

places.title: Cupra Maritima
places.description: Cupra Maritima was a coastal city of Picenum (regio V) assigned to the tribus Velina.

places.title: Cupra Montana
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Cupra Montana

places.title: Cures
places.description: Cures (also Cures Sabini) was a Sabine city in the Tiber River valley along the Via Salaria. The Romans conquered Cures in 290 B.C. under M'. Curius Dentatus and granted it status as a municipium in the tribus Sergia.

places.title: Doganella
places.description: Doganella was an important Etruscan settlement of the Albegna valley, occupied between ca. 600 and 400 B.C. The city may have comprised as many as 240 ha.

places.title: Faesulae
places.description: Faesulae (modern Fiesole) was an Etruscan foundation called Viesul, Viśl, or Vipsul. The city was conquered by Romans in 283 B.C. Sulla would settle Roman veterans there. Citizens of the town supported the conspiracy of Catiline.

places.title: Falerii
places.description: A fortified town located some 6 km from Falerii Veteres and established by the ancient Romans ca. 241 B.C.

places.title: Falerio
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Falerio

places.title: Fanum Fortunae
places.description: Fanum Fortunae, the site of a shrine to Fortuna, is first mentioned in the ancient sources in 49 B.C. when Iulius Caesar held the town. An Augustan colony was established at the site and the Romans prevailed in the Battle of Fano in A.D. 271. The town was eventually destroyed by the Ostrogoths.

places.title: Ferentium
places.description: Ferentium (modern Ferento) was a city of Etruria first mentioned in the Liber Coloniarum ca. 123 BC that became a Roman municipium after the Social War. Substantial remains of the city remain; the site was the birthplace of Otho and noted for its fine stone monuments and statues.

places.title: *Firmidianum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 *Firmidianum

places.title: Firmum Picenum
places.description: Firmum Picenum was founded as a Latin colony in 264 B.C. with 6,000 colonists. It received municipal status after 48 B.C.

places.title: Florentia
places.description: Florentia (modern Florence / Firenze) was founded as a colony for military veterans ca. 80 B.C. by Lucius Cornelius Sulla.

places.title: Fontecchio
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 F4 Fontecchio

places.title: Foruli
places.description: Foruli was a Sabine town located between Amiternum and Interocrea.

places.title: Forum Aurelii
places.description: A settlement in Etruria situated on the Via Aurelia between Centumcellae and Cosa according to the Antonine Itinerary.

places.title: Forum Cassii
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Forum Cassii

places.title: Forum Clodii
places.description: An ancient road station on the Via Clodia.

places.title: Forum Decii
places.description: A town of the Sabines mentioned by Pliny the Elder.

places.title: Forum Flaminii
places.description: A town founded in 220 B.C. by Caius Flaminius during the construction of the Via Flaminia.

places.title: Forum Novum (Vescovio)
places.description: Forum Novum was a Roman town and an early medieval bishopric. It is located in the Sabine hills and was likely founded as a market center during the Republican period. It had achieved the status of municipium by the first century A.D. The market center seems to have remained active until at least th

places.title: Forum Sempronii
places.description: An ancient Roman colony, founded in the time of Gaius Sempronius Gracchus.

places.title: Fulginiae
places.description: Fulginiae was an ancient town of Umbria, Italy, on the later line of the Via Flaminia, ca. 20 km south of Nuceria.

places.title: Galeata
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Galeata

places.title: Graviscae
places.description: The port of the Etruscan city of Tarquinia.

places.title: Grotte di Castro
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Grotte di Castro

places.title: Hatria (Picenum)
places.description: An ancient city of Picenum that may have originated as colony established by Etruscans from Adria in the Veneto region. An alternate narrative suggests that the city's origins may be as a late sixth century B.C. colony founded by Aegina.

places.title: Heba
places.description: A Roman colony that was established in the third or second century B.C., Heba lay near modern Magliano. Funerary evidence indicate previous Etruscan occupation at the site.

places.title: Helvia Ricina
places.description: An ancient settlement in Picenum at modern Villa Potenza in Marche, Comune di Macerata, Italy.

places.title: Helvillum
places.description: Helvillum was a vicus in Umbria located about 10 Roman miles from Aesis (Jesi).

places.title: Hispellum
places.description: Hispellum (modern Spello) is an ancient settlement of Umbria that became a Roman colony in the first century BC.

places.title: Histonium
places.description: Histonium, on the Adriatic coast, was a chief town of the Frentani.

places.title: Horta
places.description: The Etruscan settlement of *Hurta (the modern Orte) was close to the Vadimonis Lacus where the Romans fought, and won, two engagements against Etruscan armies.

places.title: Iguvium
places.description: An Umbrian hilltown, Iguvium is best known as the find-spot of the Iguvine Tables.

places.title: Interamna Nahars
places.description: An Umbrian center founded in the seventh century B.C. that became an important Roman municipality along the Via Flaminia.

places.title: Interamnia Praetuttiorum
places.description: Originally a settlement of the Praetuttii located at the confluence of the rivers Tordino and Vezzola (modern Teramo).

places.title: Interocrium
places.description: A Sabine town that was later known as a mansio on the course of the Via Salaria.

places.title: Interpromium
places.description: A village of the Marrucini, forming a station on the Via Claudia Valeria between Corfinium and Teate.

places.title: Lucus Feroniae
places.description: A sanctuary and grove of Feronia and an associated settlement located along the Via Tiberina in the territory of Capena.

places.title: Luni sul Mignone
places.description: Luni sul Mignone is a site with archaeological evidence for habitation in the later second millennium BC, continuing into the Italian Iron Age. Excavations conducted by the Swedish Institute in Rome (1960-1963) exposed three phases of settlement activity.

places.title: Magliano Sabina
places.description: Magliano Sabina is located in Lazio, some 50 km north of Rome and some 30 km west of Rieti.

places.title: Manliana
places.description: One of two Roman road stations with this name in Italy attested in ancient sources. The Barrington Atlas Directory localizes this one at modern Torrita di Siena.

places.title: Marsiliana d’Albegna
places.description: An ancient settlement located near the confluence of the rivers Albegna and Elsa.

places.title: Martanum
places.description: An ancient harbor of the city of Tarquinia.

places.title: Matilica
places.description: Matilica was a municipium in Umbria located near the source of the river Aesis and close to the borders of Picenum. The Liber Coloniarum identifies the settlement as one of the “Civitates Piceni.”

places.title: Mevania
places.description: Mevania (modern Bevagna) was a Roman municipium in Umbria located on the Via Flaminia. The town was enrolled in the tribus Aemilia.

places.title: Mola di Monte Gelato
places.description: An ancient settlement 30 km north of Rome that was excavated from 1986-90. An imperial villa existed on the site up until the third century AD.

places.title: Montedoro di Scapezzano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E1 Montedoro di Scapezzano

places.title: Monte S. Angelo
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monte S. Angelo

places.title: Monteferetra
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Monteferetra

places.title: Montelibretti
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Montelibretti

places.title: Monterano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Monterano

places.title: Poggio Civitate (Murlo)
places.description: An Etruscan elite complex of the seventh and sixth centuries B.C. located at Poggio Civitate, a hill adjacent to the medieval town of Murlo and about 25 km south of Siena.

places.title: Musarna
places.description: Musarna is an ancient Etruscan settlement discovered in 1849 just west of Viterbo, Italy. The École française de Rome has been conducting excavations at the site since 1983.

places.title: Nepet
places.description: Nepet had become a Roman town before 396 B.C. when Livy dubs it, along with Sutrium, as one of the "keys" to Etruria. It became a Roman colony in 383 B.C. and a municipium after the Social War.

places.title: Nequinum/Narnia
places.description: Nequinum/Narnia (modern Narni) was an ancient settlement in Umbria. It became a Latin colony in 299 BC.

places.title: Novilara
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Novilara

places.title: Nuceria
places.description: Nuceria (modern Nocera Umbra) is an ancient town in Umbria, perhaps founded in the seventh century B.C. by Camerinum.

places.title: Numana
places.description: Numana was a settlement of ancient Picenum located south of Ancona.

places.title: Nursia
places.description: Nursia was the northernmost city of the Sabines.

places.title: Ocriculum
places.description: An ancient Umbrian city that became allied with Rome in 308 B.C.

places.title: [Orcla]
places.description: [Orcla] or Norchia is an ancient Etruscan settlement located near Tarquinia and along the line of the Roman Via Clodia.

places.title: Ortona
places.description: An ancient site in Italy that most likely originates with the Frentani.

places.title: Ostia Aterni
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 G4 Ostia Aterni

places.title: Paganica
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E4 Paganica

places.title: Passo Corese
places.description: Passo Corese is located near Cures (Fara in Sabina). The site is often connected with Titus Tatius' march on Rome in 747 B.C.

places.title: Pausulae
places.description: Pausulae was a town of Picenum mentioned by Pliny the Elder. It was a Municipium of Regio V.

places.title: Perusia
places.description: A city of ancient Umbrian and Etruscan origin, Perusia aided Rome during the Second Punic War but was sieged and reduced by Octavian in the first century B.C. during campaigns against Lucius Antonius. It was rebuilt by Augustus and became Colonia Vibia Augusta Perusia quite late, in A.D. 251-3, unde

places.title: Phalacrinae
places.description: A Roman town in which the emperor Vespasian was born in A.D. 9.

places.title: Pinna
places.description: Pinna (modern Penne) was a center of the Vestini. The site came under Roman control after the Social War (89 BC).

places.title: Pisaurum
places.description: Pisaurum (modern Pésaro) was founded as a Roman colony in the territory of the Picentes in 184 BC.

places.title: Pitigliano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B3 Pitigliano

places.title: Pitino
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 Pitino

places.title: Pitinum
places.description: An ancient center of the Vestini.

places.title: Pitinum Mergens
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D1 Pitinum Mergens

places.title: Pitinum Pisaurense
places.description: An ancient settlement in Umbria, known mostly via its inclusion in the texts of Pliny the Elder and Ptolemy, as well as by means of various epigraphic evidence.

places.title: Poggio Sommavilla
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D4 Poggio Sommavilla

places.title: Polimartium
places.description: An ancient Roman settlement (modern Bomarzo in Italy).

places.title: Ponte a Buriano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B1 Ponte a Buriano

places.title: Potentia
places.description: A city settled in an area subjugated by Rome during the fourth century B.C. The local populace rebelled against Rome after the defeat at Cannae (216 B.C.), however the defeat of the Carthaginians eventually led to Potentia's reincorporation into the Roman sphere.

places.title: Prolaqueum
places.description: A statio on the road from Nuceria to Ancona.

places.title: Punta La Penna
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Punta La Penna

places.title: Reate
places.description: Reate (modern Rieti) was a major Sabine center that came to be captured by Manius Curius Dentatus in late third century B.C.

places.title: Respampani
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 B4 Respampani

places.title: Rusellae
places.description: An Etruscan city captured by Rome in 294 B.C., Rusellae's >2 mile circuit of megalithic walls represent an important early instance of stone fortification walling in the Italian peninsula.

places.title: Saena
places.description: Saena was an Etruscan city that received a Roman colony (Saena Iulia) in the time of Augustus.

places.title: S. Casciano dei Bagni
places.description: The village of San Casciano dei Bagni, located south of Siena, Italy, has been frequented since at least the first millennium BCE on account of its thermal springs with supposedly healing properties.

places.title: San Giovenale
places.description: The archaeological remains of an Etruscan settlement were discovered at San Giovenale, close to Blera, Italy, by the Swedish Institute at Rome in the 1950s and 1960s. The ancient name of the site is unknown.

places.title: S. Vittore
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 E2 S. Vittore

places.title: Sarsina
places.description: Sarsina was a town of the Umbri that was captured by Cornelius Scipio in 271 B.C. and was the birthplace of the Latin author Plautus. The necropolis at Sarsina has been extensively studied.

places.title: Sarteano
places.description: Sarteano is located between the Val d'Orcia and the Valdichiana. It is known in particular for its rich evidence of Etruscan funerary culture.

places.title: Sur Jureh
places.description: Sur Jureh (also Sur Jurʿeh, Sūr Ğurʿa) is a site in the middle Euphrates region in what was part of the ancient kingdom of Suhu. The city, which is probably to be identified with ancient Gabbāri-bānî (or Gabbāri-ibni), was situated on the north bank of the Euphrates, opposite Gleieh (which lies on t

places.title: Sena Gallica
places.description: Senonian Gauls founded Sena Gallica at the mouth of the Misa River in the fourth century B.C. This place became the site of Rome's earliest colony on the Adriatic seaboard before 280 B.C. Pompeius Magnus destroyed the city in 82 B.C.

places.title: Sentinum
places.description: An ancient town in the region of Italy now known as Le Marche, Sentinum is perhaps best known for the pivotal Battle of Sentinum of the Third Samnite War that took place nearby in 295 BC.

places.title: Sestinum
places.description: Sestinum was an ancient place in Umbria near the headwaters of the river Pisaurus. Pliny mentions the site, and its ancient name is preserved in modern toponymy.

places.title: Sorano
places.description: Sorano was a Villanovan and, later, Etruscan settlement.

places.title: Sorrina
places.description: Sorrina was a small Etruscan settlement on Viterbo's Colle di San Lorenzo, of which some traces remain. Epigraphic evidence also attests to a Roman municipium - Surrina Nova - that was likely located between Viterbo and Lake Bullicame.

places.title: Spoletium
places.description: An ancient city along the route of the Via Flaminia; an initial colony was established there in 241 BCE.

places.title: Suana
places.description: Suana (Sovana) has Etruscan origins but later became a Roman municipium. In the fifth century A.D. it became an episcopal see.

places.title: Suasa
places.description: Suasa was the site of a Roman municipium in Umbria. It lies in the Piano Volpello along a road from Cales to Sena Gallica. Alaric razed the settlement in 409.

places.title: Superaequum
places.description: One of three towns of the Paeligni which possessed municipal rights.

places.title: Sutrium
places.description: An ancient settlement along the line of what would become the Roman Via Cassia and described by Livy, together with Nepet, as one of the keys to Etruria. A Latin colony was founded at the site after the fall of Veii.

places.title: Tadinae
places.description: Tadinae (Sant'Antonio della Rasina to the west of Gualdo Tadino) is an ancient municipium of Umbria and was a road station on the Via Flaminia.

places.title: Tarchna/Tarquinii
places.description: An ancient city of Etruria and the leading city of the doudecim populi Etruriae, Tarquinia (called Tarch(u)na or Tarchna in Etruscan) was a major urban center of ancient Italy.

places.title: Teate
places.description: Originally named Teate Marrucinorum, Teate (modern Chieti) was the principal settlement of the Marrucini. Strabo attributes its origins to Arcadian Greeks.

places.title: Tifernum Mataurense
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C1 Tifernum Mataurense

places.title: Tifernum Tiberinum
places.description: An Umbrian hilltown in the floodplain of the Tiber river north of Perusia.

places.title: Tolentinum
places.description: Tolentinum was a town of Picenum that is listed as having municipal status in the Liber Coloniarum.

places.title: Trebiae
places.description: Trebiae was an ancient city of Umbria (regio IV) located near the line of the Via Flaminia. It is identified with modern Trevi, north of Spoleto in Italy.

places.title: Trebula Mutuesca
places.description: Trebula Mutuesca or Trebula Mutusca was one of two Sabine cities bearing the name Trebula.

places.title: Trevignano
places.description: Trevignano Romano, located on the shores of Lake Bracciano, lies some 47 km from Rome. Archaeological evidence for Etruscan occupation, in the form of tombs dating to the eighth - sixth centuries B.C., has been discovered to the north of the modern town. A medieval castle was built there under Innoc

places.title: Tuder
places.description: Tuder, modern Todi, is an ancient city of Umbria. Its foundation likely occurred during the eighth/seventh centuries BC, although legendary traditions associate the site with the activities of Herakles.

places.title: Tuficum
places.description: Tuficum was an ancient city of Umbria located on the Aesis river. It became a municipium of the tribus Oufentina.

places.title: Tuscana
places.description: An ancient city that traced its legendary origins to Ascanius, son of Aeneas. The site became an important Etruscan mercantile center and eventually achieved Roman municipal status in 88 B.C.

places.title: Urbs Salvia
places.description: An ancient city of Regio V (Picenum) where a Roman colony was founded in the second century B.C.

places.title: Urvinum Mataurense
places.description: Urvinum Mataurense (modern Urbino).

places.title: Velzna/*Volsinii Veteres/Urbiventus
places.description: Volsinii Veteres was one of the most powerful and important cities of Etruria, as it was the location of the important federal sanctuary located at the Fanum Voltumnae.

places.title: Verucchio
places.description: Around the modern Italian town of Verucchio (Emilia-Romagna), a number of ancient necropoleis provide evidence for iron-age civilization and craft at a presumed settlement on the site lasting into the Roman period.

places.title: Vespasiae
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vespasiae

places.title: Vettona
places.description: Vettona (modern Bettona) is an ancient settlement of Umbria located between Perusia and Mevania. Pliny the Elder lists it among the municipalities of Umbria, and it also numbered as one of the “xv Populi Umbriae".

places.title: Vicus Martis
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 D3 Vicus Martis

places.title: Vicus Matrini
places.description: Vicus Matrini was a mansio along the Via Cassia, located between Sutri and Forum Cassi. The site's name is attested on the Peutinger Table.

places.title: Vignanello
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 C4 Vignanello

places.title: Villalfonsina
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 42 H4 Villalfonsina

places.title: Visentium
places.description: Visentium (Bisenzio) was an Etruscan settlement located on the shores of Lago di Bolsena. The site has yielded especially important evidence for Iron Age and Etruscan period burials.

places.title: Vulci
places.description: Vulci (originally Velch or Velx in Etruscan) was an Etruscan city 80 km northwest of Rome. Vulci was one of the duodecim populi Etruriae.

places.title: Tell Fekheriye
places.description: Tell Fekheriye is the site of ancient Sikkan in Syria's Khabur river valley. Sikkan was part of the Aramaean kingdom of Bit Bahiani.

places.title: Monastiraki Katalimata
places.description: A refuge settlement in Crete located near the Late Minoan site of Chalasmenos.

places.title: Nea Nikomedeia
places.description: Nea Nikomedeia is a Neolithic settlement in Macedonia, dating to the seventh millennium BC.

places.title: Khirbet Beit-Bassa
places.description: An ancient fortress located in Beit Sahour, in the district of Bethlehem in Palestine.

places.title: Rofalco
places.description: A fortified Etruscan site located in the territory of Vulci.

places.title: Poliochne
places.description: A Bronze Age settlement on the island of Lemnos, Poliochne pre-dates Troy I and shows influence from the Greek mainland during Early Helladic II (ca. 2500 BC). Mycenaean horizons have also been identified.

places.title: Acqua Acetosa
places.description: A settlement along the Via Laurentina that has yielded significant evidence for protohistoric occupation, including funereal evidence of the eighth and seventh centuries B.C.

places.title: Aefula
places.description: Aefula was an ancient settlement of Latium that had disappeared by the time of Pliny the Elder, although the cult of Bona Dea there continued to flourish.

places.title: Afilae
places.description: Located in the Anio river valley to the south of Subiaco, Afilae was a municipium that was likely assigned to the tribus Aniensis.

places.title: Alba Longa
places.description: Alba Longa, located in the Alban Hills southeast of Rome, was the chief city and founder of the Latin League. Conflict with Rome caused Alba's destruction in the seventh century B.C. The legendary history of Romulus and Remus connects them to the royal lineage of the city. The ancient city is probab

places.title: Algidus
places.description: An ancient settlement of Latium located in the territory of the Aequi.

places.title: Alsium
places.description: Alsium served as a port for Caere, together with Fregenae.

places.title: Anagnia
places.description: Anagnia was a Hernican town that sided with Rome against the Volscians and later became civitas sine suffragio. By Cicero's time it received the status of municipium.

places.title: Annunziatella
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Annunziatella

places.title: Antemnae
places.description: Antemnae is an ancient Latin settlement located north of Rome near the point where the Anio and Tiber rivers intersect. Connected with Rome's early history, Antemnae was involved in episodes such as the 'Rape of the Sabine Women' and Romulus is said to have celebrated a triumph over the Antemnates i

places.title: Antium
places.description: Antium ranked as one of the most important and most powerful centers of Latium and was captured by Rome at the close of the Latin War in the fourth century B.C. Imperial Antium was well known for its number of coastal villas.

places.title: Ardea
places.description: Ardea was an ancient settlement of the Rutuli in Latium.

places.title: Aricia
places.description: Aricia is an ancient Latin settlement and a member of the Latin League.

places.title: Artena
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Artena

places.title: Buon Riposo
places.description: Buon Riposo is a small, fortified settlement covering some 2 hectares. Its fortifications date to the seventh century BCE or later.

places.title: Campo del Fico
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C3 Campo del Fico

places.title: Castel Campanile
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 A2 Castel Campanile

places.title: Le Castella
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Le Castella

places.title: Castel Madama
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Castel Madama

places.title: Castelporziano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B3 Castelporziano

places.title: Castel Savello
places.description: Castel Savello takes its name from a fifteenth-century fortress of the Savelli family at Albano Laziale. Funerary evidence associated with the Latial culture has been documented here.

places.title: Castrimoenium
places.description: A Latin settlement that became a Roman municipium.

places.title: Ciciliano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Ciciliano

places.title: Collatia
places.description: Collatia was an ancient city of Latium located between Gabii and the Anio Rover. A colony of Alba Longa, Collatia was one of the most ancient cities of Latium. Subjugated by Rome under the Tarquins, Collatia would decline during the Republican period and numbers among the lost Latin cities by the ac

places.title: Colle Monitola
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D2 Colle Monitola

places.title: Cora
places.description: A Latin center in the Monti Lepini that was already a Roman municipium by 211 B.C.

places.title: Crustumerium
places.description: An ancient town of Latium located at the headwaters of the Allia river, very close to the territory of the Sabines, Crustumerium figures in Rome's early history. The Romans conquered the site in 500 B.C. and formed the tribus Crustumina or Clustumina in 471 B.C.

places.title: Ficulea
places.description: Ficulea was an ancient city of Latium situated between Rome and Nomentum.

places.title: Fidenae
places.description: Fidenae was an ancient city of Latium.

places.title: Fregenae
places.description: An ancient town of Etruria, Fregenae was located between Alsium and the mouth of the river Tiber.

places.title: Gabii
places.description: An ancient Latin city located on the line of the Republican Via Praenestina connecting Rome to Praeneste. Gabii is allied to Rome from an early date and flourished during the archaic period, declining by the time of Augustus.

places.title: Lanuvium
places.description: Lanuvium was an important city of Latium located south of the Alban Hills. After opposing Rome at the battle of Aricia (504 B.C.) and Lake Regillus (496 B.C.), Lanuvium was captured by the Romans in 338 B.C.

places.title: Lavinium
places.description: An ancient city of Latium on the Numicus River that was founded, according to Virgil, by Aeneas.

places.title: Magliana Vecchia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Magliana Vecchia

places.title: Nettuno
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C4 Nettuno

places.title: Nomentum
places.description: The Latin town of Nomentum and Rome were linked by means of the Via Nomentana. In Livy's history the town, a member of the Latin League, is captured by Lucius Tarquinius Priscus. Nomentum was one of a number of towns captured by Tarquinius. The Romans granted the town civitas sine suffragio after 33

places.title: Norba
places.description: Norba, located in the Monti Lepini, was a member of the Latin League (ca. 499 B.C.) and became a Latin colony ca. 492 B.C. The city was destroyed in the early first century B.C.

places.title: Pometia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 D3 Pometia

places.title: Praeneste
places.description: An ancient city of central Italy, the eighth and seventh century B.C. origins of which demonstrate high-level trade contact with the Eastern Mediterranean world. The city withdrew from the Latin League (499 B.C.) and opposed Rome in the Latin war; Cincinnatus eventually subdued Praeneste. Sulla foun

places.title: La Rustica
places.description: La Rustica was a Latin site located along the Via Collatina.

places.title: S. Gennaro
places.description: A minor settlement.

places.title: S. Rufina
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Rufina

places.title: Serrone di Bove
places.description: The small hill that is known as "Il Poggio di Serrone di Bove" is located in the hinterland of ancient Norba and was the site of ancient settlement activity. Architectural remains on the site include those of a polygonal masonry sub-struction or platform as well as an ancient roadway that may be par

places.title: Setia
places.description: A Volscian settlement of the fifth century B.C. that became a Latin colony in 382 B.C.

places.title: Signia
places.description: A city of Latium Adjectum established as a Latin colony ca. 494 B.C.

places.title: La Storta
places.description: A station on the Via Cassia attested in an inscription dated to A.D. 379-383.

places.title: Sublaqueum
places.description: An ancient settlement, located at modern Subiaco in Italy, Sublaqueum was located in the territory of the Aequi that was annexed by Rome in 304 B.C.

places.title: Tibur
places.description: A Sabine town, 30 km east-north-east of Rome, Tibur was the seat of the Tiburtine Sibyl.

places.title: Tor Angela
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 Tor Angela

places.title: Torre Pascolaro (settlement)
places.description: A Final Bronze Age settlement of four to five hectares in South Etruria.

places.title: Il Torrino
places.description: An Iron Age settlement in Latium.

places.title: Trebula Suffenas
places.description: An ancient Sabine city.

places.title: Tusculum
places.description: Tusculum was a Latin city of the Alban Hills in central Italy. After 381 B.C., Tusculum became the first "municipium cum suffragio".

places.title: Valvisciolo
places.description: An Iron Age settlement and necropolis located in the Monti Lepini near the abbey of Valvisciolo, characterized by polygonal masonry terrace walls. While the ancient name of the site is unknown, various proposals have been raised, including Sulmo (Savignoni, Mengarelli) and Pometia (Ogilvie). The set

places.title: Varia
places.description: Varia (modern Vicovaro) was a settlement of the Sabines.

places.title: Veii
places.description: An important city of South Etruria located north-northwest of Rome, Veii was eventually sacked by the Romans in 396 B.C. The ancient city covered some 180 ha.

places.title: Velitrae
places.description: Velitrae (modern Velletri) was an ancient Volscian settlement. In the Roman Republican period, Velitrae was attacked by Marcus Furius Camillus (379 B.C.) and again by Cincinnatus (377 B.C.); the Romans controlled the site by 365 B.C. The gens Octavia hailed from the city and a youthful Octavian spen

places.title: Vicus Alexandri
places.description: A settlement at the third milestone of the Via Ostiensis.

places.title: Nichoria
places.description: Located in Messenia, Nichoria was a site with important Bronze Age and Iron Age phases.

places.title: Tell Beydar
places.description: Tell Beydar (ancient Nabada) is an archaeological site in NE Syria that was first settled ca. 2600 BC.

places.title: Sahab
places.description: A farming village southeast of Amman, Jordan, inhabited from the late Neolithic Period through the sixth century BCE, and briefly inhabited again from the eleventh-thirteenth centuries; now the site of the modern town of Sahab.

places.title: Colle Rasto Settlement
places.description: A site to the west of modern Praeneste in Italy where surface material, remains of structures, and graves were discovered in the 19th century. These finds provide evidence for a settlement possibly dating to as early as the fifth or fourth century BCE but with likely occupation throughout the subseq

places.title: Sawtry
places.description: The modern-day site of a Roman-British settlement dates from the second to fourth centuries AD.

places.title: Kār-Tukultī-Ninurta
places.description: A place from the TAVO Index

places.title: Rablê
places.description: A town mentioned in Neo-Assyrian sources; the modern site is Riblah, located ca. 35 km south of Ḥomṣ.

places.title: Abella
places.description: Abella was an ancient settlement of Campania of Samnite origin.

places.title: Acerrae
places.description: Acerrae was an ancient Oscan city of Campania, perhaps originally named Akeru. The Romans granted it civitas sine suffragio in 332 BC.

places.title: Aequana
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Aequana

places.title: Aesernia
places.description: An ancient settlement (modern Isernia in Italy)

places.title: Afragola
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Afragola

places.title: Agnone
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Agnone

places.title: Al(l)ifae
places.description: An ancient town of either Oscan or Samnite origin situated in the Volturno river valley.

places.title: Aletrium
places.description: A Hernican hill town that formed part of a sixth-century B.C. defensive league against Volscian and Samnite aggression and allied itself to Tarquinius Superbus. Rome eventually took Aletrium in 306 B.C.; by the first century B.C., the site was a Roman municipium.

places.title: Alfedena
places.description: A Samnite settlement occupying a strategic location in the valley of the Sangro river.

places.title: Amalfitana Civitas
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Amalfitana Civitas

places.title: Angitiae Lucus
places.description: Angitiae Lucus refers to the grave of Angitia, a divine figure of the Marsi tribe.

places.title: Antinum
places.description: A town of the Marsi in the valley of the Liris river.

places.title: Aquinum
places.description: Aquinum was a municipium by the time of Cicero. It was thought to be the place of birth for the satirist Juvenal and the emperor Pescennius Niger.

places.title: Arpinum
places.description: An ancient center that originated as early as the seventh century B.C. that became a civitas sine suffragio in 305 B.C. Arpinum was the birthplace of Caius Marius and Marcus Tullius Cicero.

places.title: Arx Fregellana
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Arx Fregellana

places.title: Atella (Campania)
places.description: A city of Campania located between Capua and Neapolis.

places.title: Aufidena
places.description: A probable Samnite center, the Romans captured Aufidena in 298 BC. It only became a municipium after 49 B.C.

places.title: Aversa
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Aversa

places.title: Baiae
places.description: A Roman seaside community on the Bay of Naples that included thermal springs.

places.title: Beneventum/Maleventum
places.description: Beneventum/Maleventum (modern Benevento) was an ancient city of Campania of Samnite origin.

places.title: Boscoreale
places.description: A settled area of Campania that is especially well known for the Roman country villas of the first century BC that were destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in A.D. 79.

places.title: Boscotrecase
places.description: Located on the southern slopes of Vesuvius, Boscotrecase is a Campanian site destroyed by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79. Numerous opulent villas are known in the area by way of archaeological exploration.

places.title: Bovianum
places.description: Bovianum was a Samnite center and the capital of the Pentri tribe. It received Roman municipium status ca. 87 B.C. By the late first century A.D. it was occupied by veterans of Legio XI and known as the "colonia Bovianum Undecimanoruin".

places.title: Buca
places.description: Buca was an ancient settlement of the Frentani.

places.title: Caiatia
places.description: A Samnite town that eventually became a Roman municipium of the tribus Falerna ca. 89 B.C.

places.title: Caieta
places.description: Caieta was a town of ancient Latium located on the Tyrrhenian Sea coast between Tarracina and Formiae.

places.title: Calatia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Calatia

places.title: Cales (Campania)
places.description: Cales was an ancient city of Campania of Ausonian origins. The Romans captured the town in 335 B.C. and established a colony there.

places.title: Campobasso
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Campobasso

places.title: Capreae
places.description: Settlement on the island of Capreae.

places.title: Capriati
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F3 Capriati

places.title: Capua
places.description: An important ancient city of Campania with Villanovan and Etruscan origins.

places.title: Carovilli
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Carovilli

places.title: Carsioli
places.description: An ancient settlement along the Via Valeria, Carsioli was established as a Latin colony in the territory of the Aequi ca. 298 BC.

places.title: Cascano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Cascano

places.title: Casilinum
places.description: A settlement located in the border region between the ager Falernus and the ager Campanus, north of Capua.

places.title: Casinum
places.description: A Volscian hilltop settlement that became a Roman colony in 312 B.C.

places.title: Castro dei Volsci
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 D3 Castro dei Volsci

places.title: Castropignano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Castropignano

places.title: Castrum Novum
places.description: Castrum Novum was a colonia maritima established on the coast of Etruria.

places.title: Caudium
places.description: A city of Samnium located between Capua and Beneventum. In 321 B.C. the Samnites under C. Pontius encamped there before defeating the Romans at the battle of the Caudine Forks.

places.title: Cereatae Marianae
places.description: Cereatae Marianae, purported to have been the birthplace of Caius Marius, is thought to have been located where the 13th-century abbey church of Casamari now stands (in the modern province of Frosinone, Lazio, Italy).

places.title: Chiauci
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Chiauci

places.title: Circeii 1
places.description: Circeii received a Latin colony ca. 390 B.C. The remains on the site include an enclosure wall built in polygonal masonry. "Circeii 1" refers to the earlier Roman colony founded at the eastern side of Monte Circeo. The settlement eventually moved to the western side of the peninsula.

places.title: Civitanova
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Civitanova

places.title: Cliternia
places.description: A city of northern Apulia.

places.title: Colle Mitra
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E1 Colle Mitra

places.title: Cretone
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 C1 Cretone

places.title: Cumae/Kyme (Campanian)
places.description: An ancient settlement of Campania, Cumae was the first Greek colony established on the Italian mainland in the eighth century BC.

places.title: Dikaiarcheia/Puteoli
places.description: A maritime city of Campania situated on the Phlegrean Peninsula. The settlement started as a Greek colony and became a Roman colony under the name Puteoli in 194 B.C.

places.title: Duronia
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Duronia

places.title: Fabrateria Nova
places.description: Fabrateria Nova received a Roman colony in 124 B.C. that was dispatched by Caius Gracchus. The relationship between Fabrateria Nova and the earlier Volscian site of Fabrateria Vetus remains unclear. The favored location for Fabrateria Nova is at S. Giovanni Incarico, where the Liri and Sacco rivers

places.title: Fabrateria Vetus
places.description: Fabrateria Vetus was a Volscian settlement that surrendered to Rome in 424 B.C.

places.title: Fagifulae
places.description: Fagifulae was a center of the Pentrian Samnites.

places.title: Ferentinum
places.description: A Hernican town along the Via Latina that the Romans captured in 364 B.C. Later in the Republican period (after 195 B.C.) the city received Roman municipal status.

places.title: Ferrazzano
places.description: A fortified ancient hilltop, Ferrazzano is usually identified as a Samnite site.

places.title: Formiae
places.description: An ancient settlement of likely Greek origin along the Via Appia. Cicero was assassinated near Formiae (now Formia) in 43 B.C.

places.title: Fregellae
places.description: Fregellae was a city of Latium Adjectum that became a Roman colony in 328 B.C., but was subsequently captured by the Samnites; a Roman presence was re-established in 313 B.C. Loyal to Rome during the Second Punic War, Fregellae revolted in 125 B.C. and the site was razed.

places.title: Fregellanum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Fregellanum

places.title: Frosolone
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Frosolone

places.title: Frusino
places.description: Frusino (modern Frosinone) was a town in Latium along the Via Latina that was originally a Volscian settlement.

places.title: Fundi
places.description: Fundi achieved civitas sine suffragio after the Latin War in 338 B.C.

places.title: Gioia dei Marsi
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E2 Gioia dei Marsi

places.title: ‘Iovis Lareni’
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F1 ‘Iovis Lareni’

places.title: Iuvanum
places.description: A Roman municipium founded in 87 BC after the Social War, Iuvanum sits on the site of a pre-existing Samnite settlement that occupies an upland plateau.

places.title: Kupelternum/Cubulteria
places.description: Kupelternum/Cubulteria was an ancient Samnite settlement.

places.title: Ligures Baebiani
places.description: Ligures Baebiani was a Ligurian settlement in Samnium.

places.title: Marruvium
places.description: Ancient Marruvium was the principal city of the Italic tribe of the Marsi.

places.title: Mignano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Mignano

places.title: Minturnae
places.description: Originally an Ausonian town that fought against Rome in 314 B.C., Minturnae became a colony in 296 B.C. The site is located on the Garigliano river (ancient Liris) and served an important economic function. The Via Appia passes through the city.

places.title: Misenum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Misenum

places.title: Monte Cavallerizzo
places.description: Monte Cavallerizzo is a fortified Samnite center - perhaps dating to the fourth century B.C. - located in close proximity to the sanctuary at Vastogirardi.

places.title: Monte Frascara
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Monte Frascara

places.title: Monte Monaco di Gioia

places.title: Monte S. Croce

places.title: Monte Saraceno di Cercemaggiore
places.description: Archaeological excavations on the area of the summit of Monte Saraceno have documented the remains of an imposing, fortified high-altitude settlement which has a second walled area within it.

places.title: Monte Vairano
places.description: At Monte Vairano are the remains of a fortified center of the Pentrian Samnites.

places.title: Monteverde
places.description: The eleventh century monastery of Santa Maria di Monteverde sits atop and reuses elements of Roman and pre-Roman settlements on the hilltop.

places.title: Montevetrano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Montevetrano

places.title: Morroni
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Morroni

places.title: Nola
places.description: The city of Nola (Nuvlana) is considered one of the oldest in Campania. Under Augustus the settlement became a Roman colony; it was the spot where Augustus died in A.D. 14.

places.title: Nuceria (Alfaterna)
places.description: Nuceria (Alfaterna) (modern Nocera Inferiore) is an ancient settlement in Campania. In pre-Roman times this was the chief settlement of the Sarnus river valley.

places.title: Oplontis
places.description: An ancient place (modern Torre Annunziata in Italy), lying between Pompeii and Herculaneum and buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in 79 CE. Its ancient name is known only from Peutinger's Roman Map.

places.title: Oratino
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Oratino

places.title: Pagus Meflanus
places.description: Pagus Meflanus was likely located in the Apennines to the northeast of Beneventum.

places.title: Pagus Sarclanus
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Pagus Sarclanus

places.title: *Pallanum
places.description: An ancient settlement of the Frentani located on Monte Pallano.

places.title: Panapio/Punicum
places.description: The ancient settlement of Panapio/Punicum corresponds to present-day Santa Marinella, Rome, Italy.

places.title: Parthenope/Neapolis
places.description: Founded as Parthenope by Greeks in the eighth century B.C., the site eventually gave rise to Neapolis in the sixth century B.C. and was one of the most prominent cities of Magna Graecia. Modern-day Naples, Italy.

places.title: Pescolanciano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F2 Pescolanciano

places.title: Pian di Sorrento
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Pian di Sorrento

places.title: Pithekoussai
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E4 Pithekoussai

places.title: Pompeii
places.description: An ancient city of Campania destroyed by the volcanic eruption of Mt. Vesuvius in A.D. 79, Pompeii was named as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

places.title: Porticone
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G2 Porticone

places.title: Privernum
places.description: A Volscian center that Rome reportedly destroyed in the late fourth century B.C.

places.title: Punta Chiarito
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E4 Punta Chiarito

places.title: Pyrgi
places.description: Pyrgi is an ancient Etruscan port city on the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy. A Roman colony was established at the site by 191 B.C. In 1964 the bi-lingual 'Pyrgi Plaques' were discovered during the course of excavations.

places.title: Rufrae
places.description: A Samnite settlement at the margins of Campania.

places.title: Saepinum
places.description: An ancient town of Samnium captured by the Romans in 293 B.C., located on the road between Beneventum and Corfinium.

places.title: Salernum
places.description: A city of Campania with Osco-Etruscan origins that became a Roman colony in 197 B.C.

places.title: S. Angelo d’Ogliara
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 S. Angelo d’Ogliara

places.title: S. Apollinare
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 S. Apollinare

places.title: S. Buono
places.description: A fortified town near Chieti in the Abruzzo, the ancient phases of S. Buono include evidence for an indigenous sacred site of the later first millennium BC. Among the finds are votive objects dedicated to Herakles.

places.title: S. Marzano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 S. Marzano

places.title: S. Valentino Torio
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 S. Valentino Torio

places.title: S. Vincenzo al Volturno
places.description: S. Vincenzo al Volturno is a multi-period settlement. In pre-Roman times a phase of Samnite occupation has been identified. By the fifth century A.D. the site was occupied by a large agricultural estate (villa) that was abandoned in the later fifth century, only to be replaced by a Christian church.

places.title: S. Vittore
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 S. Vittore

places.title: Sarno
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Sarno

places.title: Saticula
places.description: Saticula was a Samnite site in Campania that received a Latin colony in 313 B.C.

places.title: Sinues(s)a/Sinope
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 E3 Sinues(s)a/Sinope

places.title: Sora
places.description: An ancient city of Latium located in the valley of the Liris River that likely had Volscian origins. The Romans captured the city in 345 BCE and later established a colony there in 303 BCE after the Second Samnite War.

places.title: Speluncae
places.description: An ancient grotto, associated with the nearby Villa Tiberii, at the modern Italian town of Sperlonga.

places.title: Striano
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 G4 Striano

places.title: Suessa Aurunca
places.description: The ancient center of the Aurunci, Suessa Aurunca was abandoned in 337 B.C. for a more favorable site (modern Sessa) where a Latin colony was established in 313 B.C.

places.title: Suessula
places.description: Suessula was an important ancient city of Campania.

places.title: Sulmo
places.description: A chief settlement of the Peligni that was ravaged by the Carthaginians during the Second Punic War.

places.title: Surrentum
places.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 44 F4 Surrentum

places.title: Tarracina(e)/Anxur
places.description: A strategic Volscian city that had come under Roman control by 509 B.C.; a Roman citizen colony was established there in 329 B.C. The site is particularly notable for the remains of the terraced sanctuary of Iuppiter Anxur.

places.title: Teanum Sidicinum
places.description: Teanum Sidicinum (modern Teano) was the capital of the Oscan-speaking Sidicini tribe. The city likely submitted to Rome after 334 B.C.

places.title: Telesia
places.description: An ancient Samnite city located in the valley of the Calor river.

places.title: Terventum
places.description: Terventum was the site of a Roman municipium established in the territory of the Pentrian Samnites.

places.title: Terzigno

places.title: Treba
places.description: Treba (modern Trevi nel Lazio) was originally a settlement of the Aequi.

places.title: Urbana

places.title: Venafrum
places.description: Venafrum was an ancient town of Campania.

places.title: Verulae
places.description: Verulae is an ancient city that became a Roman municipium in 90 B.C. Modern Veroli in Italy.

places.title: Volturnum
places.description: Volturnum was located at the mouth of the Volturno River.

places.title: Andeualo
places.description: A Spanish village located in the southwest of the province of Huelva that belonged to the kingdom of Alfonso X. It is now known as El Andévalo.

places.title: Tell Sukas
places.description: The ancient Shuksi or Suksi, the archaeological site of Tell Sukas is a Late Bronze Age tell located south of Jableh, Syria. The site was situated at the center of the fertile plain of Jableh and had access to two natural harbors.

places.title: Salteras
places.description: An ancient and medieval Spanish village located north of Sevilla that belonged to the thirteenth-century kingdom of Alfonso X.

places.title: Kurşun Kalesi
places.description: Remains of an ancient hilltop settlement, with houses, agricultural processing areas, a stoa, a temple, and some ancient Greek inscriptions located within the modern Turkish municipality of Yeğenli (Mersin province). places.title: Castrum Invi
places.description: An Italic site located at the mouth of the Incastro river and in the territory of Ardea.

places.title: Castellina del Marangone
places.description: A small fortified coastal settlement in Etruria occupied from the tenth century B.C. to the first century B.C.

places.title: El Kab
places.description: An ancient Egyptian site with settlements dating back to prehistoric and Pharaonic times. The site also features rock-cut tombs from the 18th Dynasty and two temples primarily in use from the Early Dynastic period to the Ptolemaic period.

places.title: Aeclanum
places.description: An ancient settlement in Samnium that came to be associated with the Hirpini.

places.title: Aequum Tuticum/Equus Tuticus

places.description: Prusias ad Mare/Kios was an ancient Greek city on the Propontis. The city joined the Aetolian League and was destroyed by Philip V of Macedon. Prusias I of Bithynia rebuilt the site, naming it for himself.

places.description: Tell es-Sakan is the site of an Egyptian and Canaanite maritime settlement located in what is now the Gaza Strip at the mouth of Wadi Ghazzeh.

places.title: Hacheston
places.description: Site of a Romano-British settlement dating from the first-fourth centuries CE, located near modern Wickham Market in Suffolk.

places.title: Körzüt (Arapzengi) Kalesi
places.description: Körzüt is the modern Turkish name of an Urartean fortress situated on a rock spur at the southern end of the Muradiye/Berkri plain, about 3 km north of the modern village of Uluşar (Korsot/Gortsut), in the Muradiye district of Van province in Turkey. According to an inscription of the Urartean King

places.title: Molino San Vincenzo
places.description: Field surveys, geophysical prospection, as well as targeted research and training excavations, have revealed the remains of a mid- to late- imperial rural settlement with evidence for agricultural activity. However, the earliest finds (e.g., bucchero) date to the sixth/fifth century B.C., indicating

places.title: Umm al-Biyara
places.description: Sandstone massif just west of Petra occupied in the late Iron Age, possibly with some reoccupation in the Hellenistic period.

places.title: Byzantium
places.description: An ancient Greek settlement at the southern end of the Bosphorus where modern-day Istanbul, Turkey now stands. It flourished and grew throughout the Greek and Roman periods. The city was renamed Constantinopolis (q.v.) and much expanded by the fourth-century emperor, Constantine and his successors.
